:::{#def-n-gram-model}
#### $N$-gram model

An **$N$-gram model**, for an [integer](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/number-systems.html#def-integers) $N \ge 1$,
is a [sequence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-sequence) $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ of [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv)
in which each variable depends on the earlier ones
only through the $N - 1$ variables just before it:
for every $t > N$ and all values $x_1, \ldots, x_t$
with $\P(X_1 = x_1, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1}) > 0$,

$$
\P(X_t = x_t \mid X_1 = x_1, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1})
= \P(X_t = x_t \mid X_{t-N+1} = x_{t-N+1}, \ldots, X_{t-1} = x_{t-1}).
$$

:::
